sections.title: 1. Technical Introduction (Purpose, Scope, Definitions)
sections.body: This Software Requirements Specification (SRS) defines the technical requirements for the Hospital EMR Patient Management System (Patient Portal). The purpose of this document is to establish a baseline for the design, development, and verification of the system, ensuring alignment with healthcare industry standards. The scope encompasses the technical architecture, functional capabilities, and non-functional constraints required to securely manage patient data within the EMR ecosystem. Key definitions include 'EMR' (Electronic Medical Record) and 'Patient Portal' (the user-facing interface for patient data access and management). Note: The source document excerpt is highly condensed; specific module boundaries and detailed user roles are currently open items requiring stakeholder input.

sections.title: 2. Overall Description & System Architecture
sections.body: The system operates as a secure web-based portal integrated with the hospital's core EMR infrastructure. The architecture is designed to facilitate secure data exchange between the patient-facing interface and the backend EMR database. The system must maintain strict data integrity and confidentiality, adhering to the operational boundaries of a healthcare environment. Specific architectural diagrams and component interactions are not detailed in the source excerpt and are flagged as open items for the design phase.

sections.title: 3. Functional Requirements
table: System shall allow authorized patients to view their medical records via the portal.
System shall implement secure user authentication mechanisms for portal access.

sections.title: 4. Non-Functional Requirements (Performance, Security, Reliability mapped to domain standards)
sections.body:
The system must meet the following non-functional requirements, strictly adhering to the HIPAA compliance framework and domain-specific NFR benchmarks:

1. **Performance**: The system shall maintain a P95 latency of less than 250ms for standard portal interactions, per the healthcare domain NFR benchmark.
2. **Security (Encryption at Rest)**: Per HIPAA §164.312(a)(2)(iv), the system shall implement robust encryption for all Protected Health Information (PHI) stored at rest. This includes database encryption and file storage encryption to ensure data confidentiality in the event of a physical or logical breach.
3. **Security (Audit Logging)**: Per HIPAA §164.312(b), the system shall implement comprehensive audit logging capabilities. The system must record all access, modification, and deletion events related to PHI, including user identity, timestamp, and action type. These logs must be tamper-evident and retained for a minimum of six years.
4. **Reliability**: The system shall maintain high availability to ensure continuous access to critical patient data.

sections.title: 5. External Interface Requirements (APIs, UI, Hardware)
sections.body: The system shall integrate with the existing Hospital EMR backend via secure APIs. The User Interface (UI) shall be responsive and accessible, adhering to web accessibility standards. Specific API endpoints, hardware dependencies, and third-party service integrations are not detailed in the source excerpt and are listed as open items requiring technical stakeholder definition.

sections.title: 6. System Constraints & Compliance Verification
sections.body: The system is constrained by the need to operate within the hospital's existing network infrastructure and security policies. Compliance verification will be conducted through regular security audits, penetration testing, and HIPAA compliance reviews. The implementation of encryption at rest and audit logging (as specified in Section 4) is a mandatory constraint for system deployment. Any deviation from these compliance requirements will result in a system rejection during the verification phase.
